Cc: procurement@medicore.com

Subject: Pilot packaging question — can we decouple 'Advanced Rerank' from Tier B?

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency and the suggested batching settings. We are finalizing scope for a 90-day pilot and had one packaging question from procurement and product: is it possible to make the Advanced Rerank feature optional for Tier B so we can run with Tier B core throughput but add Rerank only if we hit accuracy targets?

Specifically, procurement wants clarity on:
- If Rerank is decoupled, how does that affect the unit pricing?
- Would there be a separate add-on SKU or credits model for the feature?
- Any constraints for switching the feature on mid-pilot (downtime/rollouts)?

Can you share a short checklist or recommended approach — procurement is asking for a one-page summary we can attach to the SOW.

Appreciate it,

Sara

Subject: Re: Pilot packaging question — can we decouple 'Advanced Rerank' from Tier B?

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the ledger. Short answer: yes, we can decouple it, and we have two pragmatic ways to do it. Below is the one-page checklist you can attach to the SOW; I’m copying Karthik and Ben for pricing/ops details and Lauren for rollout/runbook notes.

One-page checklist: Tier reweighting + optional feature decoupling (pilot)
1) Packaging model options (pick one):
   a) Add-on SKU: Rerank as a metered add-on priced per 1k rerank requests. Fastest to invoice.
   b) Feature credit bucket: prepaid credit pool consumed when Rerank is called; useful if usage is spiky.
2) Mid-pilot activation:
   - No restart required. Feature flag flip + model variant routing; few seconds of ramp while caches populate.
   - Recommend rolling enable at 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic over 1 hour if accuracy is unknown.
3) Pricing impact on Tier B:
   - If Add-on SKU chosen: Tier B base price unchanged; separate line item for rerank.
   - If credit bucket: can offer a small discount for a committed bucket (e.g., 10–15% off list for 3-month commitment).
4) SLA/rollback:
   - Auto-fallback to non-rerank path on error (no downtime).
   - Rollback via feature flag in Console (immediate).
5) Contract language to include:
   - Definition of "Rerank unit" (per API call that invokes reranking).
   - Activation window and one-time migration charge (if customer requests on-call deployment support).

I’ve attached a proposed tier matrix for pricing scenarios. Karthik/Ben — can you propose numbers for the Add-on SKU and a 3-month committed credit example? Lauren — any operational caveats to call out?

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging question — can we decouple 'Advanced Rerank' from Tier B?

Thanks Priya — quick pricing proposals below so procurement has something concrete. Ben and I discussed both options and show ballpark numbers; we can tighten them after we see a 2-week telemetry sample.

Option A — Add-on SKU (metered):
- Rerank unit = per completed rerank API call (approx cost drivers: extra tokens + rerank model compute).
- List: $0.40 per 1k rerank calls.
- If committed 3-month volume >= 1M rerank calls -> discounted price $0.30 per 1k.

Option B — Credit bucket (prepaid):
- 100k rerank credits = $28 (equivalent to $0.28 per 1k).
- 10% additional discount for auto-renew of bucket.

Operational notes:
- Activation has no downtime; cache warm-up may add a 1–2% latency blip for first few minutes. Not material for the pilot.
- We recommend the credit bucket for spiky usage (mobile bursts).

Ben — call out any minimums or billing mechanics for procurement.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Hi all — adding billing mechanics and a small procurement-friendly clause.

Billing mechanics (Add-on SKU):
- Invoiced monthly as a separate line. Usage measured daily, billed monthly.
- Minimum monthly charge during pilot = $500 (waived if MediCore signs a 3-month committed bucket).

Contract clause (suggested):
"Customer may enable the Advanced Rerank add-on during the Pilot period. If enabled, usage will be billed at the agreed add-on rate. Redwood will provide an activation runway and rollback mechanism; enabling the feature will not constitute a material change to the Pilot scope unless accompanied by a mutually agreed SOW amendment."

Lauren — for runbook: confirm fallback path and how we surface metrics to MediCore (we propose a shared dashboard + daily telemetry digest during the first week).

Thanks,

Sara — quick operational confirmation and next steps.

Runbook highlights:
- Pre-activation: we enable a feature flag in the Console and stage a model variant with rerank logic in canary. No infra changes.
- Activation window: staged canary (5% traffic) for 30 minutes, then 25% for 30 minutes, then 100%. We monitor error rate, 99th p90 latency, and a small accuracy signal (A/B labeled set) during canary.
- Rollback: immediate feature-flag flip; systems automatically route to non-rerank path.
- Visibility: we will provision a shared dashboard (token-level latency, rerank hit-rate, cost-per-1k) and a daily digest for first 5 business days after activation.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Sara/procurement picks pricing option (Add-on SKU or Credit bucket) by 2026-09-06.
2) If credit bucket chosen, we send a 3-month credit invoice and activate the bucket on payment clearance.
3) If add-on chosen, we add the clause Ben drafted into the SOW and set a $500 pilot minimum unless MediCore commits to the 3-month bucket.

Sara, happy to hop on a 20-min call tomorrow afternoon to walk procurement through the SOW wording and the dashboard.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Technical Customer Success | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
